newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal government to sell firm to private investors.
newsitem.headline: Nepal government to sell firm to private investors.

text.p: The Nepali government will sell a state-owned firm to private investors as part of its liberalisation drive, finance ministry officials said on Tuesday.

They said the private investors would pay 95.1 million rupees ($1.67 million) for a 65 percent stake in the state-owned Agricultural Tools Factory (ATF). The share price has been fixed at 55 rupees for a 10-rupee share "The money will be paid in seven instalments within the next 39 months," a finance ministry statement said.
Officials said 30 percent shares would be sold to the Nepali public through the capital market and five percent stake will go to the employees of the factory.
"This will be done on an appropriate time," said Tanka Khanal, in charge of privatisation department at the Finance Ministry.
The initial amount of 10 million rupees has already been paid, he added.
The Finance Ministry statement said an agreement for the deal on the ATF had already been signed with the buyers.
ATF, which makes agricultural tools like pump sets, threshers, shovels and tractor trailers, was shut down last year following management problems.
Nepal has privatised 11 state-owned firms and liquidated two companies after it embarked on a policy of liberalisation to buoy its sagging economy, one of the world's 10 poorest.

The government has also off-loaded 10 percent shares in Nepal Bank Limited, the kingdom's premier financial institution, reducing its holding to a minority stake of 41 percent, Khanal told Reuters. ($1= 56.75 Nepali rupees)
